```text
# models/migrations — versioned schema changes

**Read when:** you changed a persisted struct under `models/`, or a migration test fails.
**Not here:** the runtime engine -> `models-db.md`; running the suite -> `testing.md`.

## Responsibilities

An ordered, append-only list of schema migrations. Each has an integer id; the database records how
far it has got, and startup applies whatever is missing. `services/versioned_migration` is what
invokes this at boot.

## Key files

| Path | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `models/migrations/migrations.go` | the ordered slice, `newMigration`, `minDBVersion`, `Migrate`, `EnsureUpToDate`, `GetCurrentDBVersion`, `ExpectedDBVersion` |
| `models/migrations/v1_27/v343.go` | a minimal add-columns migration — the shape to copy |
| `models/migrations/base/db.go` | `RecreateTable`, `RecreateTables`, `DropTableColumns`, `ModifyColumn` |
| `models/migrations/migrationtest/tests.go` | `PrepareTestEnv`, `MainTest` for migration tests |
| `models/migrations/fixtures/Test_<FuncName>/` | per-test fixture directory, named after the test |

## Conventions & invariants

- A migration is one `newMigration(<id>, "<description>", v1_27.FuncName)` entry **appended at the
  bottom** of the slice in `migrations.go`. Order is the schema history; never insert in the
  middle, never renumber.
- The implementation lives in the current version subpackage as `v<id>.go` — migration 342 is
  `models/migrations/v1_27/v342.go` — with the function exported and named for what it does.
- Signature is `func(x db.EngineMigration) error`, or with a leading `context.Context` when the
  migration needs one. `newMigration` accepts either.
- The database version is *the last migration's id + 1*. `minDBVersion` is 70 (Gitea 1.5.3):
  installs older than that must upgrade through an intermediate release first.
- **A migration declares its own local copy of every struct it touches, inside the function**, with
  only the columns it cares about. `v342.go` declares a local `ActionRun` holding just the three
  new columns. Never import the live model from `models/` — the model keeps evolving, and a
  migration must describe the schema *as of its own moment* forever.
- Partial table changes use `x.SyncWithOptions(xorm.SyncOptions{IgnoreDropIndices: true,
  IgnoreConstrains: true}, new(Foo))` rather than plain `Sync`, so unrelated indices and
  constraints survive (`docs/guidelines-backend.md`).
- A column added to an existing table takes `NOT NULL DEFAULT <value>`
  (`models/migrations/v1_27/v343.go`): the default fills existing rows in the same `ALTER TABLE`.
  Without it the column is nullable and old rows hold NULL (`models/migrations/v1_27/v332.go`),
  which `WHERE col = 0` does not match. `NOT NULL` with no default fails on a populated table.
- New `.go` files carry a copyright header with the current year (`AGENTS.md`).

## Recipes

**Add a migration.**

1. Change the real struct in its `models/<domain>/` package.
2. Create `models/migrations/v1_27/v<next id>.go` with an exported function and a local struct copy
   holding only the affected columns.
3. Append `newMigration(<next id>, "<description>", v1_27.FuncName)` to the bottom of the slice in
   `migrations.go`.
4. Add `v<next id>_test.go` beside it, using `migrationtest.PrepareTestEnv`; put any fixtures in
   `models/migrations/fixtures/Test_<FuncName>/`.
5. `make test-migration`.

**Change a column type or drop columns.** Use `base.ModifyColumn` or `base.DropTableColumns` rather
than raw SQL — they handle the per-driver differences. `base.RecreateTable` is the last resort for
changes some drivers cannot express.

## Gotchas

- **Never edit a migration that has shipped.** Installs that already ran it will not run it again,
  so the edit silently applies to new installs only and the two diverge. Add a new migration.
- Registering a model with `db.RegisterModel` creates the table on a *fresh* install only. Existing
  installs need the migration — this is the most common way a change works locally and breaks on
  upgrade.
- Migration tests use their own harness (`migrationtest`), not `models/unittest`. The fixture
  directory name must match the test function name exactly or no fixtures load.
- `migrationtest` loads fixtures through `models/unittest/fixtures_loader.go` → `NewFixturesLoader`,
  which skips, without an error, any table whose model is not registered. Blank-import the owning
  package and assert the row count, as `models/migrations/v1_27/v343_test.go` does.
- `make test-migration` is a separate target from `make test-backend`; a migration can be broken
```

```text
func Test_AddCloseReasonToIssue(t *testing.T) {
	type Issue struct {
		ID       int64 `xorm:"pk autoincr"`

	}
}
```

```text
// Copyright 2024 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package activities

import (
	"context"

	"gitea.dev/models/db"
	issues_model "gitea.dev/models/issues"
	access_model "gitea.dev/models/perm/access"
	repo_model "gitea.dev/models/repo"
	"gitea.dev/models/unit"
	user_model "gitea.dev/models/user"
	"gitea.dev/modules/container"
	"gitea.dev/modules/log"
	"gitea.dev/modules/util"

	"xorm.io/builder"
)

// FindNotificationOptions represent the filters for notifications. If an ID is 0 it will be ignored.
type FindNotificationOptions struct {
	db.ListOptions
	IDs               []int64
	UserID            int64
	RepoID            int64
	IssueID           int64
	Status            []NotificationStatus
	Source            []NotificationSource
	UpdatedAfterUnix  int64
	UpdatedBeforeUnix int64
	GroupByRepo       bool // order by repository full name first, so each repository's rows are contiguous across pages
}

// ToCond will convert each condition into a xorm-Cond
func (opts FindNotificationOptions) ToConds() builder.Cond {
	cond := builder.NewCond()
	if len(opts.IDs) > 0 {
		cond = cond.And(builder.In("notification.id", opts.IDs))
	}
	if opts.UserID != 0 {
		cond = cond.And(builder.Eq{"notification.user_id": opts.UserID})
	}
	if opts.RepoID != 0 {
		cond = cond.And(builder.Eq{"notification.repo_id": opts.RepoID})
	}
	if opts.IssueID != 0 {
		cond = cond.And(builder.Eq{"notification.issue_id": opts.IssueID})
	}
	if len(opts.Status) > 0 {
		if len(opts.Status) == 1 {
			cond = cond.And(builder.Eq{"notification.status": opts.Status[0]})
		} else {
			cond = cond.And(builder.In("notification.status", opts.Status))
		}
	}
	if len(opts.Source) > 0 {
		cond = cond.And(builder.In("notification.source", opts.Source))
	}
	if opts.UpdatedAfterUnix != 0 {
		cond = cond.And(builder.Gte{"notification.updated_unix": opts.UpdatedAfterUnix})
	}
	if opts.UpdatedBeforeUnix != 0 {
		cond = cond.And(builder.Lte{"notification.updated_unix": opts.UpdatedBeforeUnix})
	}
	return cond
}

func (opts FindNotificationOptions) ToJoins() []db.JoinFunc {
	if opts.GroupByRepo {
		return []db.JoinFunc{func(sess db.Engine) error {
			sess.Join("INNER", "repository", "repository.id = notification.repo_id")
			return nil
		}}
	}
	return nil
}

func (opts FindNotificationOptions) ToOrders() string {
	if opts.GroupByRepo {
		// case-insensitive like the repository filter's list; the id tiebreak keeps rows from moving between pages
		return "LOWER(repository.owner_name), repository.lower_name, notification.updated_unix DESC, notification.id DESC"
	}
	return "notification.updated_unix DESC"
}
```

```text
210	func filterNotificationsByRepoAccess(ctx stdCtx.Context, doer *user_model.User, notifications activities_model.NotificationList) (activities_model.NotificationList, []int, error) {
211		failures := make([]int, 0)
212		for i, notification := range notifications {
213			if notification.Repository == nil {
214				continue
215			}
216			perm, err := access_model.GetIndividualUserRepoPermission(ctx, notification.Repository, doer)
217			if err != nil {
218				return nil, nil, err
219			}
220			if !perm.HasAnyUnitAccessOrPublicAccess() {
221				failures = append(failures, i)
222			}
223		}
224		return notifications.Without(failures), failures, nil
225	}

227	// notificationGroup is one repository's section of the grouped notification list
228	type notificationGroup struct {
229		Repo          *repo_model.Repository
230		UnreadCount   int64 // across every page of the view, not only this one
231		Continued     bool  // the section started on the previous page

233	}

235	// groupNotificationsByRepo splits a page already ordered by repository into one section per repository
236	func groupNotificationsByRepo(notifications activities_model.NotificationList, prevPageRepoID int64, unreadCounts map[int64]int64) []*notificationGroup {
237		groups := make([]*notificationGroup, 0, 4)
238		for _, n := range notifications {
239			if len(groups) == 0 || groups[len(groups)-1].Repo.ID != n.RepoID {
240				groups = append(groups, &notificationGroup{
241					Repo:        n.Repository,
242					UnreadCount: unreadCounts[n.RepoID],
243					Continued:   len(groups) == 0 && n.RepoID == prevPageRepoID,
244				})
245			}
246			last := groups[len(groups)-1]
247			last.Notifications = append(last.Notifications, n)
248		}
249		return groups
250	}
```

```go
package v1_27

import (

func AddReasonToNotification(x db.EngineMigration) error {
	type Notification struct {
		Reason int `xorm:"SMALLINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0"` // 0 is "Other": why an existing notification was sent isn't known

	}, new(Notification))
```

```bash
	UserID      int64
	RepoID      int64

	Source      int
	IssueID     int64
	CommentID   int64

	UpdatedUnix int64

	}
}
```

```bash
func parseNotificationFilter(ctx *context.Context) notificationFilter {
```

```text
// Copyright 2017 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package activities_test

import (
	"context"
	"testing"

	activities_model "gitea.dev/models/activities"
	"gitea.dev/models/db"
	issues_model "gitea.dev/models/issues"
	"gitea.dev/models/unittest"
	user_model "gitea.dev/models/user"
	"gitea.dev/modules/util"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
)

func TestCreateOrUpdateIssueNotifications(t *testing.T) {
	assert.NoError(t, unittest.PrepareTestDatabase())
	issue := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: 1})

	assert.NoError(t, activities_model.CreateOrUpdateIssueNotifications(t.Context(), issue.ID, 0, 2, 0, activities_model.NotificationReasonSubscribed))

	// User 9 is inactive, thus notifications for user 1 and 4 are created
	notf := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &activities_model.Notification{UserID: 1, IssueID: issue.ID})
	assert.Equal(t, activities_model.NotificationStatusUnread, notf.Status)
	unittest.CheckConsistencyFor(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: issue.ID})

	notf = unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &activities_model.Notification{UserID: 4, IssueID: issue.ID})
	assert.Equal(t, activities_model.NotificationStatusUnread, notf.Status)
}

func TestNotificationsForUser(t *testing.T) {
	assert.NoError(t, unittest.PrepareTestDatabase())
	user := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: 2})
	notfs, err := db.Find[activities_model.Notification](t.Context(), activities_model.FindNotificationOptions{
		UserID: user.ID,
		Status: []activities_model.NotificationStatus{
			activities_model.NotificationStatusRead,
			activities_model.NotificationStatusUnread,
		},
	})
	assert.NoError(t, err)
	if assert.Len(t, notfs, 3) {
		assert.EqualValues(t, 5, notfs[0].ID)
		assert.Equal(t, user.ID, notfs[0].UserID)
		assert.EqualValues(t, 4, notfs[1].ID)
		assert.Equal(t, user.ID, notfs[1].UserID)
		assert.EqualValues(t, 2, notfs[2].ID)
		assert.Equal(t, user.ID, notfs[2].UserID)
	}
}

func TestNotification_GetRepo(t *testing.T) {
	assert.NoError(t, unittest.PrepareTestDatabase())
	notf := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &activities_model.Notification{RepoID: 1})
	repo, err := notf.GetRepo(t.Context())
	assert.NoError(t, err)
func TestFindNotificationsGroupByRepo(t *testing.T) {
	assert.NoError(t, unittest.PrepareTestDatabase())

	ids := func(opts activities_model.FindNotificationOptions) []int64 {
		nls, err := db.Find[activities_model.Notification](t.Context(), opts)
		assert.NoError(t, err)
		ids := make([]int64, 0, len(nls))
		for _, n := range nls {
			ids = append(ids, n.ID)
		}
		return ids
	}

	// #5 (user2/repo2) is user2's newest, so it leads the ungrouped list but follows all of user2/repo1 when grouped
	assert.Equal(t, []int64{5, 4, 3, 2}, ids(activities_model.FindNotificationOptions{UserID: 2}))
	assert.Equal(t, []int64{4, 3, 2, 5}, ids(activities_model.FindNotificationOptions{UserID: 2, GroupByRepo: true}))

	page2 := ids(activities_model.FindNotificationOptions{UserID: 2, GroupByRepo: true, ListOptions: db.ListOptions{Page: 2, PageSize: 2}})
	assert.Equal(t, []int64{2, 5}, page2) // the order holds across pages
}
func TestCountNotificationsByRepo(t *testing.T) {
	assert.NoError(t, unittest.PrepareTestDatabase())

	unread, err := activities_model.CountNotificationsByRepo(t.Context(), activities_model.FindNotificationOptions{
		UserID: 2,
		Status: []activities_model.NotificationStatus{activities_model.NotificationStatusUnread},
	})
	assert.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, map[int64]int64{1: 1, 2: 1}, unread)

	filtered, err := activities_model.CountNotificationsByRepo(t.Context(), activities_model.FindNotificationOptions{UserID: 2, RepoID: 1})
	assert.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, map[int64]int64{1: 3}, filtered)

	none, err := activities_model.CountNotificationsByRepo(t.Context(), activities_model.FindNotificationOptions{
		UserID: 2,
		Source: []activities_model.NotificationSource{activities_model.NotificationSourceCommit},
	})
	assert.NoError(t, err)
```

```text
func TestParseNotificationFilter(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		query    string
		expected notificationFilter
		active   bool
		qs       string
	}{
		{"", notificationFilter{}, false, ""},
		{"?repo=2&source=pull", notificationFilter{RepoID: 2, Source: "pull"}, true, "repo=2&source=pull"},
		{"?source=unknown", notificationFilter{}, false, ""},
		{"?repo=abc", notificationFilter{}, false, ""},
		{"?repo=-5&source=commit", notificationFilter{Source: "commit"}, true, "source=commit"},
		{"?group=repo", notificationFilter{GroupByRepo: true}, false, "group=repo"}, // grouping is not a filter
		{"?group=repo&repo=2", notificationFilter{RepoID: 2, GroupByRepo: true}, true, "group=repo&repo=2"},
		{"?group=bogus", notificationFilter{}, false, ""},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		t.Run(c.query, func(t *testing.T) {
			ctx, _ := contexttest.MockContext(t, "notifications"+c.query)
			filter := parseNotificationFilter(ctx)
			assert.Equal(t, c.expected, filter)
			assert.Equal(t, c.active, filter.IsActive())
			assert.Equal(t, c.qs, filter.queryString())
		})
	}

	opts := notificationFilter{RepoID: 2, Source: "pull"}.findOptions(7)
	assert.EqualValues(t, 7, opts.UserID)
	assert.EqualValues(t, 2, opts.RepoID)
	assert.Equal(t, []activities_model.NotificationSource{activities_model.NotificationSourcePullRequest}, opts.Source)
}
func TestNotificationViewLink(t *testing.T) {
	filter := notificationFilter{RepoID: 2, Source: "pull"}
	assert.Equal(t, "/notifications", notificationViewLink("", 1, notificationFilter{}))
	assert.Equal(t, "/notifications", notificationViewLink("unread", 0, notificationFilter{})) // both spellings of the unread tab are one view
	assert.Equal(t, "/notifications?type=read", notificationViewLink("read", 1, notificationFilter{}))
	assert.Equal(t, "/notifications?page=3&repo=2&source=pull&type=read", notificationViewLink("read", 3, filter))
	assert.Equal(t, "/notifications?repo=2&source=pull", notificationViewLink("bogus", 1, filter))
	assert.Equal(t, "/notifications?group=repo&page=2&type=read", notificationViewLink("read", 2, notificationFilter{GroupByRepo: true}))
}
```

```text
func TestNotificationGroupByRepo(t *testing.T) {
	defer tests.PrepareTestEnv(t)()

	// user2 fixtures: #3 pinned (repo 1), #4 unread (repo 1), #5 unread (repo 2), #2 read (repo 1); #5 is the newest
	session := loginUser(t, "user2")

	type section struct {
		Header string
		IDs    []string
	}
	sectionsAt := func(t *testing.T, link string) ([]section, *HTMLDoc) {
		resp := session.MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", link), http.StatusOK)
		doc := NewHTMLParser(t, resp.Body)
		var sections []section
		doc.doc.Find("#notification_table .notification-group").Each(func(_ int, g *goquery.Selection) {
			s := section{Header: strings.Join(strings.Fields(g.Find(".notification-group-header").Text()), " ")}
			g.Find(".notifications-item").Each(func(_ int, row *goquery.Selection) {
				s.IDs = append(s.IDs, row.AttrOr("id", ""))
			})
			sections = append(sections, s)
		})
		return sections, doc
	}

	t.Run("SectionsByRepoNewestFirst", func(t *testing.T) {
		sections, _ := sectionsAt(t, "/notifications?group=repo")
		assert.Equal(t, []section{
			{"user2/repo1 1 unread", []string{"notification_4", "notification_3"}}, // the pinned row stays in its repository
			{"user2/repo2 1 unread", []string{"notification_5"}},
		}, sections)
	})

	t.Run("OffIsUnchanged", func(t *testing.T) {
		sections, doc := sectionsAt(t, "/notifications")
		assert.Empty(t, sections)
		var ids []string
		doc.doc.Find("#notification_table .notifications-item").Each(func(_ int, s *goquery.Selection) {
			ids = append(ids, s.AttrOr("id", ""))
		})
		assert.Equal(t, []string{"notification_5", "notification_4", "notification_3"}, ids)
	})

	t.Run("UnreadCountCoversTheRepository", func(t *testing.T) {
		sections, _ := sectionsAt(t, "/notifications?type=read&group=repo")
		assert.Equal(t, []section{{"user2/repo1 1 unread", []string{"notification_3", "notification_2"}}}, sections) // #4 is unread, though listed on the other tab

		sections, _ = sectionsAt(t, "/notifications?group=repo&source=commit")
		assert.Empty(t, sections) // nothing matches, so no headers either
	})

	t.Run("ContinuedAcrossPages", func(t *testing.T) {
		// a third unread row makes three pages of one, since the pager counts unread rows only and pinned #3 is extra
		extra := &activities_model.Notification{UserID: 2, RepoID: 2, Status: activities_model.NotificationStatusUnread, Source: activities_model.NotificationSourceRepository, UpdatedBy: 1}
		require.NoError(t, db.Insert(t.Context(), extra))
		defer func() {
			_, err := db.DeleteByID[activities_model.Notification](t.Context(), extra.ID)
			assert.NoError(t, err)
		}()
		extraID := fmt.Sprintf("notification_%d", extra.ID) // the newest row, so it leads user2/repo2
```

```go
// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package integration

import (
	"net/http"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	activities_model "gitea.dev/models/activities"
	"gitea.dev/models/db"
	issues_model "gitea.dev/models/issues"
	repo_model "gitea.dev/models/repo"
	"gitea.dev/models/unittest"
	user_model "gitea.dev/models/user"
	"gitea.dev/modules/test"
	issue_service "gitea.dev/services/issue"
	"gitea.dev/tests"

	"github.com/PuerkitoBio/goquery"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

// the notification queue is immediate in tests, so each event has stored its notifications when the call returns
func TestNotificationReason(t *testing.T) {
	defer tests.PrepareTestEnv(t)()

	// user4 watches user2/repo1; user5 doesn't
	user2 := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: 2})
	user4 := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: 4})
	repo1 := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &repo_model.Repository{ID: 1})
	reasonOf := func(userID, issueID int64) activities_model.NotificationReason {
		return unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &activities_model.Notification{UserID: userID, IssueID: issueID}).Reason
	}

	t.Run("ReviewRequestedOutranksALaterComment", func(t *testing.T) {
		pull := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: 2})
		_, err := issue_service.ReviewRequest(t.Context(), pull, user2, nil, user4, true)
		require.NoError(t, err)
		assert.Equal(t, activities_model.NotificationReasonReviewRequested, reasonOf(4, pull.ID)) // #52 AC1

		_, err = issue_service.CreateIssueComment(t.Context(), user2, repo1, pull, "a comment every watcher hears about", nil)
		require.NoError(t, err)
		assert.Equal(t, activities_model.NotificationReasonReviewRequested, reasonOf(4, pull.ID)) // #52 AC2
	})

	t.Run("Assigned", func(t *testing.T) {
		issue := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: 5})
		removed, _, err := issue_service.ToggleAssigneeWithNotify(t.Context(), issue, user2, user4.ID)
		require.NoError(t, err)
		require.False(t, removed)
		assert.Equal(t, activities_model.NotificationReasonAssigned, reasonOf(4, issue.ID)) // #52 AC1
	})

	t.Run("MentionedAndSubscribed", func(t *testing.T) {
		issue := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: 1})
		_, err := issue_service.CreateIssueComment(t.Context(), user2, repo1, issue, "cc @user5", nil)
		require.NoError(t, err)
		assert.Equal(t, activities_model.NotificationReasonMentioned, reasonOf(5, issue.ID))   // #52 AC1
		assert.Equal(t, activities_model.NotificationReasonSubscribed, reasonOf(4, issue.ID)) // #52 AC1 a watcher
	})
}

func TestNotificationSort(t *testing.T) {
	defer tests.PrepareTestEnv(t)()

	// user2's notifications: #2 read, #3 pinned and #4 unread in user2/repo1, #5 unread in user2/repo2; #5 is the newest
	set := func(id int64, reason activities_model.NotificationReason, source activities_model.NotificationSource) {
		_, err := db.GetEngine(t.Context()).ID(id).Cols("reason", "source").Update(&activities_model.Notification{Reason: reason, Source: source})
		require.NoError(t, err)
	}
	set(2, activities_model.NotificationReasonSubscribed, activities_model.NotificationSourceIssue)
	set(3, activities_model.NotificationReasonReviewRequested, activities_model.NotificationSourcePullRequest)
	set(4, activities_model.NotificationReasonOther, activities_model.NotificationSourceIssue)
	set(5, activities_model.NotificationReasonMentioned, activities_model.NotificationSourceIssue)

	session := loginUser(t, "user2")
	type row struct{ ID, Reason string }
	rowsAt := func(t *testing.T, link string) ([]row, *HTMLDoc) {
		resp := session.MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", link), http.StatusOK)
		doc := NewHTMLParser(t, resp.Body)
		var rows []row
		doc.doc.Find("#notification_table .notifications-item").Each(func(_ int, s *goquery.Selection) {
			rows = append(rows, row{s.AttrOr("id", ""), strings.TrimSpace(s.Find(".notification-reason").Text())})
		})
		return rows, doc
	}

	t.Run("Reason", func(t *testing.T) {
		rows, doc := rowsAt(t, "/notifications?sort=reason")
		assert.Equal(t, []row{
			{"notification_3", "Review requested"}, // #52 AC9 the pinned row sorts with the rest
			{"notification_5", "Mentioned"},
			{"notification_4", ""}, // #52 AC4 "Other" has no label
		}, rows)
		assert.Equal(t, "Sort: Reason", strings.TrimSpace(doc.doc.Find(`[data-test-id="notification-sort"] > .text`).Text()))

		rows, _ = rowsAt(t, "/notifications?type=read&sort=reason")
		assert.Equal(t, []row{{"notification_3", "Review requested"}, {"notification_2", "Subscribed"}}, rows)
	})

	t.Run("Type", func(t *testing.T) {
		rows, _ := rowsAt(t, "/notifications?sort=type")
		assert.Equal(t, []row{{"notification_5", "Mentioned"}, {"notification_4", ""}, {"notification_3", "Review requested"}}, rows) // #52 AC5 issues, then pull requests
	})

	t.Run("NewestByDefaultWithLabels", func(t *testing.T) {
		rows, doc := rowsAt(t, "/notifications?sort=bogus")
		assert.Equal(t, []row{{"notification_5", "Mentioned"}, {"notification_4", ""}, {"notification_3", "Review requested"}}, rows) // #52 AC6, and Decision 7's labels
		assert.Equal(t, "Sort", strings.TrimSpace(doc.doc.Find(`[data-test-id="notification-sort"] > .text`).Text()))
	})

	t.Run("InsideRepositoryGroups", func(t *testing.T) {
		rows, doc := rowsAt(t, "/notifications?group=repo&sort=reason")
		assert.Equal(t, []row{{"notification_3", "Review requested"}, {"notification_4", ""}, {"notification_5", "Mentioned"}}, rows) // #52 AC8
		assert.Equal(t, 2, doc.doc.Find(".notification-group").Length())
	})

	t.Run("LinksKeepSort", func(t *testing.T) {
		_, doc := rowsAt(t, "/notifications?sort=reason&group=repo&source=issue&perPage=1") // two pages, so there are pagination links
		for _, c := range []struct{ selector, attr string }{
			{".small-menu-items a.item", "href"}, // Unread and Read tabs
			{`[data-test-id="notification-filter-repo"] .menu a.item`, "href"},
			{`[data-test-id="notification-filter-type"] .menu a.item`, "href"},
			{`[data-test-id="notification-group-repo"]`, "href"},
			{".pagination a.item[href]", "href"},
			{"form.notifications-buttons", "action"}, // single-row status actions
			{"#notification_div", "data-bulk-url"},
		} {
			found := doc.doc.Find(c.selector)
			require.NotZero(t, found.Length(), c.selector)
			found.Each(func(_ int, s *goquery.Selection) {
				assert.Contains(t, s.AttrOr(c.attr, ""), "sort=reason", c.selector) // #52 AC7
			})
		}
		clearFilters := doc.doc.Find(".flex-text-block a.ui.button").FilterFunction(func(_ int, s *goquery.Selection) bool {
			return strings.TrimSpace(s.Text()) == "Clear filters"
		})
		assert.Equal(t, "/notifications?group=repo&sort=reason", clearFilters.AttrOr("href", "")) // a view setting, not a filter

		var sortLinks []string
		doc.doc.Find(`[data-test-id="notification-sort"] .menu a.item`).Each(func(_ int, s *goquery.Selection) {
			sortLinks = append(sortLinks, s.AttrOr("href", ""))
		})
		assert.Equal(t, []string{
			"/notifications?repo=0&source=issue&group=repo&perPage=1",
			"/notifications?repo=0&source=issue&group=repo&sort=reason&perPage=1",
			"/notifications?repo=0&source=issue&group=repo&sort=type&perPage=1",
		}, sortLinks)
	})

	t.Run("InPlaceRefreshKeepsSort", func(t *testing.T) {
		rows, _ := rowsAt(t, "/notifications?sort=reason&div-only=true")
		assert.Equal(t, "notification_3", rows[0].ID)

		resp := session.MakeRequest(t, NewRequestWithValues(t, "POST", "/notifications/status?type=unread&page=1&sort=reason", map[string]string{
			"notification_id":     "4",
			"notification_action": "pin",
		}), http.StatusOK)
		var ids []string
		NewHTMLParser(t, resp.Body).doc.Find("#notification_table .notifications-item").Each(func(_ int, s *goquery.Selection) {
			ids = append(ids, s.AttrOr("id", ""))
		})
		assert.Equal(t, []string{"notification_3", "notification_5", "notification_4"}, ids) // #52 AC7 still by reason
	})

	t.Run("RedirectsKeepSort", func(t *testing.T) {
		resp := session.MakeRequest(t, NewRequestWithValues(t, "POST", "/notifications/bulk?type=read&sort=type", map[string]string{
			"action":           "mark_as_unread",
			"notification_ids": "2",
		}), http.StatusOK)
		redirect := test.ParseJSONRedirect(resp.Body.Bytes()).Redirect
		require.NotNil(t, redirect)
		assert.Equal(t, "/notifications?sort=type&type=read", *redirect) // #52 AC7

		resp = session.MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "POST", "/notifications/purge?sort=type"), http.StatusSeeOther)
		assert.Equal(t, "/notifications?sort=type", test.RedirectURL(resp))
	})
}
```

```text
)

// ReviewRequest add or remove a review request from a user for this PR, and make comment for it.
func ReviewRequest(ctx context.Context, issue *issues_model.Issue, doer *user_model.User, permDoer *access_model.Permission, reviewer *user_model.User, isAdd bool) (comment *issues_model.Comment, err error) {
	err = isValidReviewRequest(ctx, reviewer, doer, isAdd, issue, permDoer)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	if isAdd {
		comment, err = issues_model.AddReviewRequest(ctx, issue, reviewer, doer, false)
	} else {
		comment, err = issues_model.RemoveReviewRequest(ctx, issue, reviewer, doer)
	}

	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	if comment != nil {
		notify_service.PullRequestReviewRequest(ctx, doer, issue, reviewer, isAdd, comment)
	}

	return comment, err
}

// isValidReviewRequest Check permission for ReviewRequest
func isValidReviewRequest(ctx context.Context, reviewer, doer *user_model.User, isAdd bool, issue *issues_model.Issue, permDoer *access_model.Permission) error {
	if reviewer.IsOrganization() {
		return issues_model.ErrNotValidReviewRequest{
			Reason: "Organization can't be added as reviewer",
			UserID: doer.ID,
			RepoID: issue.Repo.ID,
		}
	}
	if doer.IsOrganization() {
		return issues_model.ErrNotValidReviewRequest{
			Reason: "Organization can't be doer to add reviewer",
			UserID: doer.ID,
			RepoID: issue.Repo.ID,
		}
	}
```

```markdown
Closes #52

## What changed

Every notification now stores **why** it was sent: Review requested, Assigned, Mentioned or Subscribed. The Notifications page has a new **Sort** dropdown with Newest (the default), Reason and Type, next to the Repository and Type filters. Each row except "Other" shows its reason as a small label.

- **Model** (`models/activities`):
  - `Notification` gets a `Reason` column. Its value is its rank: Other 0, Subscribed 1, Mentioned 2, Assigned 3, Review requested 4 (Decision 6).
  - When an event updates an existing notification, the reason only changes if the new one ranks higher (Decision 2), so a later comment doesn't turn "Review requested" into "Subscribed".
  - `FindNotificationOptions.Sort` adds `reason DESC` or `source` to the query's order. When #117's grouping is on, it applies after the repository name.
- **Migration** `v345`: adds `reason SMALLINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`, so existing notifications are "Other" and nothing else about them changes (Decision 3).
- **Notification service** (`services/uinotification/notify.go`):
  - Each queue item carries a reason. Review requests, assignments and the mention lists set their own.
  - Items with no reason (the watchers and participants broadcast, and any items queued before the upgrade) are stored as Subscribed.
  - `NewPullRequest` used to put mentioned users in the same set as watchers. It now pushes them separately, so a mentioned watcher is stored as Mentioned.
  - Repository transfer notifications skip the queue and stay "Other", as AC1 now says.
- **Router** (`routers/web/user/notification.go`): `sort=reason` or `sort=type` is parsed into the existing `notificationFilter`, the same way #117 added `group`, so the purge redirect, the bulk action redirect and the in-place refresh keep it. Any other value is ignored, which means newest first.
- **Templates**:
  - The Sort dropdown is built like #50's filter dropdowns.
  - `sort` is added to every link that already carried `group`: the tabs, both filters, both "Clear filters" links, the purge form, the single-row status forms and the bulk URL. Pagination already carries it.
  - The reason label is in `notification_item.tmpl`, so the flat and grouped lists both show it.
  - 9 new strings in `locale_en-US.json`.

## Why

Notifications are one row per thread and didn't record why they were sent, so there was no way to put "your review is requested" ahead of "a repository you watch had a comment". This PR covers every acceptance criterion in #52:

- **AC1:** review requests, assignments, mentions and watching or participating store Review requested, Assigned, Mentioned and Subscribed. Repository transfers store Other.
- **AC2:** an existing notification only takes a reason that ranks higher.
- **AC3:** the migration gives existing notifications "Other" and changes nothing else.
- **AC4:** Sort: Reason orders Review requested, Assigned, Mentioned, Subscribed, Other, newest first inside each. Every row except "Other" shows its label.
- **AC5:** Sort: Type orders issues, pull requests, commits, repositories, newest first inside each.
- **AC6:** with no sort or an unknown one, the list is newest first, in the same order as before.
- **AC7:** `sort` survives tab switches, both filters, grouping on and off, paging, single-row read and pin, bulk actions, "Mark all as read" and the in-place refresh.
- **AC8:** with grouping on, sections stay A–Z and the sort applies inside each one.
- **AC9:** pinned notifications are sorted with the rest.

## How it was tested

### Test strategy

- **The ranking and the "only raise" rule** are model logic, so they're tested against the model.
- **Sorting** is a query, so it's also tested at the model level, with grouping and paging.
- **Parsing `sort` and building the redirect link** are pure functions, so they're unit tests.
- **Which event stores which reason** depends on the notifier, the queue and the model working together. In integration tests the queue is `immediate`, so those tests drive real service calls (a review request, an assignment, comments with and without a mention, a new pull request) and check the stored reason.
- **Whether every link and redirect keeps `sort`** only shows in the rendered page, so that's an integration test, built like #117's `LinksKeepGrouping`.

| AC | Test |
| --- | --- |
| AC1 | Integration `TestNotificationReason`: `ReviewRequestedOutranksALaterComment`, `Assigned`, `MentionedAndSubscribed`, `MentionedWatcherOfANewPullRequest` (fails without the `NewPullRequest` change); `TestCreateOrUpdateIssueNotificationsReason` |
| AC2 | `TestCreateOrUpdateIssueNotificationsReason` (lower doesn't replace higher, higher does); integration `ReviewRequestedOutranksALaterComment` (a later comment keeps "Review requested") |
| AC3 | `Test_AddReasonToNotification` (every existing row is "Other"; every other column is unchanged) |
| AC4, AC9 | `TestFindNotificationsSort`; integration `TestNotificationSort/Reason` (order, labels, the pinned row sorted with the rest, the read tab) |
| AC5 | `TestFindNotificationsSort`; integration `TestNotificationSort/Type` |
| AC6 | `TestFindNotificationsSort` (no sort and an unknown sort); `TestParseNotificationFilter` (`?sort=bogus`); integration `NewestByDefaultWithLabels` |
| AC7 | `TestParseNotificationFilter`, `TestNotificationViewLink` (`sort` cases); integration `LinksKeepSort`, `InPlaceRefreshKeepsSort`, `RedirectsKeepSort` |
| AC8 | `TestFindNotificationsSort` (grouped, and across pages); integration `InsideRepositoryGroups` |

## CI / manual verification

Run in WSL (Debian) on this branch:

- `go test` for `TestCreateOrUpdateIssueNotifications`, `TestCreateOrUpdateIssueNotificationsReason`, `TestFindNotificationsSort`, `TestFindNotificationsGroupByRepo`, `TestNotificationsForUser`, `TestCountNotificationsByRepo` (`./models/activities/`), and the notification tests in `./routers/web/user/`: pass.
- `make test-migration`: pass, including `Test_AddReasonToNotification`.
- `make test-integration#TestNotification`: pass. That's the 4 `TestNotificationReason` and 7 `TestNotificationSort` subtests, plus the existing `TestNotificationFilters` (#50), `TestNotificationBulkActions` (#51) and `TestNotificationGroupByRepo` (#117).
- Playwright `notification-bulk.test.ts` and `notification-group.test.ts` on Chromium and Firefox: 4/4 pass with the new dropdown and labels on the page.
- `make lint-go lint-templates lint-editorconfig`: clean.
- CI runs on this PR and must pass before merging.

## Design

Decisions 1–5 are in #52's spec, which controlled-opposition reviewed. Decisions 6–8 were added during implementation, each with its alternatives:

- **Decision 6:** store the reason as a number equal to its rank (from the spec review). Sorting is then `ORDER BY reason DESC`, and "only raise" is a single `>`.
- **Decision 7:** show the reason label in every sort, not only under Sort: Reason.
- **Decision 8:** pick the sort from a dropdown next to the filters.

The spec review's note 1 (repository transfers) is answered in AC1: they store "Other".

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:**
- **A reason never goes back down** (Decision 2), so "Review requested" stays after the review is done or the request is removed. That's the trade-off the spec chose over tracking read state.
- **The reason numbers are part of the schema** (Decision 6). A future reason that should rank between two existing ones needs a migration to renumber.
- **Items in the notification queue during an upgrade** have no reason and are stored as Subscribed, as Decision 1 planned.

**Encountered:**
- **`UpdatedBy` never changes on an unread notification.**
  - `updateIssueNotification` (`models/activities/notification.go`) passes `"update_by"` to `Cols()`, but the column is `updated_by`, and xorm silently ignores the unknown name.
  - I confirmed it with a throwaway test: after an event by user 5, an unread notification still had `updated_by` 1.
  - It's outside #52, so I left it alone. It's worth its own bug issue.
- **Sort: Type's "Commits" group is always empty.** Gitea never creates commit notifications. #50's "Commits" filter has the same gap. I kept it so the sort follows the filter's order.
- **The pager's total still counts only the tab's status, not pinned rows** (noted in #120). Sorting doesn't change that.
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-27 00:09:47Z)**_

The bug is in `updateIssueNotification` (`models/activities/notification.go`). This is the function that runs when a notification for a thread already exists and a new event happens on that thread:

```go
// But we need update update_by so that the notification will be reorder
var cols []string
if notification.Status == NotificationStatusRead {
    notification.Status = NotificationStatusUnread
    notification.CommentID = commentID
    cols = []string{"status", "update_by", "comment_id"}
} else {
    notification.UpdatedBy = updatedByID
    cols = []string{"update_by"}          // ← the column is "updated_by"
}
_, err = db.GetEngine(ctx).ID(notification.ID).Cols(cols...).Update(notification)
```

**What's wrong:**
- `Cols(...)` tells xorm which columns to write; any column not listed is left alone.
- The real column is `updated_by` (from the field `UpdatedBy`), but the code says `"update_by"`, without the "d".
- xorm doesn't raise an error for a name that matches no column. It just matches nothing, so `updated_by` is never written.
- In the unread branch, the code sets `notification.UpdatedBy` in memory, but that value never reaches the database.
- In the read branch it doesn't even set `UpdatedBy`, so fixing the typo alone wouldn't help there.

**How I proved it:** a throwaway test took user 2's unread notification #4 (`updated_by` = 1) and ran an event by user 5 on that issue. Afterwards `updated_by` was still 1. I deleted the test afterwards.

**Why nobody noticed:**
- The comment says the update is needed "so that the notification will be reorder". But the reordering comes from a different column: `UpdatedUnix` has xorm's `updated` tag, so xorm sets it to the current time on every `Update` call, whatever `Cols` lists. The list still moves the notification to the top, just not for the reason the comment gives.
- Nothing reads `UpdatedBy` today. It isn't shown on the page, and I found no code that reads it.
- The one other place that writes it, `setNotificationStatus` (line 465), spells it correctly as `"updated_by"`. So it gets set when *you* read or pin a notification, but not when someone else's event updates it.

**What it means:**
- The stored "who last caused this notification" value goes stale.
- It's harmless today, but any future feature that reads it (for example "updated by @user" on the page, or in the API) would show the wrong person.

**The fix,** if someone takes it on as a separate bug issue: change `"update_by"` to `"updated_by"` in both branches, set `UpdatedBy` in the read branch too, and add a test that an event updates `updated_by`. Upstream Gitea has the same bug, so it could also be a small PR to upstream for the course's extra-credit option.

I kept it out of #52 because it isn't part of the spec, and changing it in this PR would mix an unrelated fix into a feature. That's why it's listed under **Encountered**.

1	# AI assistance disclosure — required format
2	
3	Course rule, not an upstream Gitea one. Every contributor discloses their own AI use per issue,
4	**even when no AI was used**. Source: the course AI Log Instructions page and `CONTRIBUTING.md`
5	(AI Contribution Policy). Two separate places, both required. The rest of the PR and issue
6	format is in `COURSE-WORKFLOW.md`.
7	
8	## 1. A comment on the issue
9	
10	Posted by each contributor on the **issue** they worked, once their work is done. One comment per
11	person — never edit someone else's. Add later sessions by editing your own table.
12	
13	```markdown
14	### AI Assistance — @your-github-username
15	
16	**Role in this issue:** Implementation
17	
18	| # | Tool | Log | What AI helped with |
19	|---|---|---|---|
20	| 1 | claude-code | [2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl.md](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/blob/main/ai-logs/sprint1/YourName/2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl.md) | Confirmed the files found during concept location, drafted the template change and tests, ran them |
21	
22	**Attachments:** [2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl/](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/tree/main/ai-logs/sprint1/YourName/2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl)
23	```
24	
25	- **Role** is one of Implementation, Code review, Testing, Other — pick the ones that apply and
26	  delete the rest, do not leave the slash list in place.
27	- **Tool** is the tool's name, e.g. `claude-code`, `claude-web`.
28	- **Log** is a full `https://github.com/...` link to the filed log. Relative paths break in issue
29	  comments. File naming is in `ai-logs/README.md`.
30	- **Attachments** only when the log has a companion folder; otherwise drop the line.
31	- **No AI used?** Keep the heading and role line and write `No AI used` in place of the table.
32	
33	## 2. A short section in the pull request description — no log link
34	
35	Reviewers read the PR, and the review rubric scores "AI transparency", so the PR says how AI was
36	used and how you verified it. It does **not** link or cite the AI log: from Sprint 1 on, logs are
37	referenced in **issue comments only**, never in PR descriptions or PR comments (Sprint 1 page, D5).

49	## Rules that make a disclosure wrong
50	
51	- **Placeholders left in**: `@your-github-username` or the full `Implementation / Code review /
52	  Testing / Other` list means the comment was pasted unread.
53	- **A log link in a PR description or PR comment.** Log links live in the issue comment only.
54	- **A log link that 404s.** Until the log is merged to `main`, link the branch that holds it; switch
55	  to the `main` link once merged.

218-
219:The person who resolved a medium issue draws a class diagram and a sequence diagram for it. Several
220-small issues that together equal one medium issue are drawn together instead. Files:
221-
222:- `docs/sprint2/diagrams/<issue#>-<github-username>-class.png` (or `.pdf`)
223:- `docs/sprint2/diagrams/<issue#>-<github-username>-sequence.png` (or `.pdf`)
224:- `docs/sprint2/diagrams/<issue#>-<github-username>.md`, which embeds both and answers the Q&A
225-
226:What the diagrams need:
227-
228-- Show the existing code found during concept location and impact analysis, and the new or changed
229-  code, and tell the two apart with a legend, colour or label.
230-- Show only the fields and methods that matter to the issue.
231:- Annotate the diagrams with the key design decisions and calls. Diagrams without annotations lose
232-  points.
233:- Add a short note on how Go maps to UML: structs, interfaces, and embedding.
234:- The `.md` follows the course template: `# Issue #<N> -- <title>`, `## Class Diagram`,
235:  `## Sequence Diagram`, `## Q&A`, each diagram embedded with
236:  `![Class diagram](<issue#>-<github-username>-class.png)` under its heading. The Q&A has 3
237:  class-diagram questions, 3 sequence-diagram questions and 1 question on AI use, answered "N/A" if
238-  no AI was used. The questions, copied from the Sprint 2 page:
239-
240-```markdown
241:**Class diagram:**
242-
243:1. Among all the classes shown in the diagram, which 1--2 are most central to understanding the codebase and solving the issue? Explain what role each one plays.
244:2. What is the most significant relationship shown in the diagram? Explain what it represents in the system and why it matters for understanding the solution.
245-3. Looking back at your implementation, is there anything in this design you would change, and why?
246-
247:**Sequence diagram:**
248-
249-1. What user action or system event starts the sequence, and what is the expected outcome when it completes successfully?
250-2. Identify the 2--3 most important steps in the sequence. For each one, describe what is happening and note whether it involves existing code or new/modified code from your solution.
251:3. What error cases or alternative paths are not shown in the diagram, and why did you leave them out?
252-
253-**Cross-cutting:**
254-
255:4. If you used AI to create or check any part of the diagrams, describe what it produced, what you verified against the actual code, and what you had to correct or add. If AI was not used, write "N/A."
256-```
257-

```text
The diagram uses UML notation for TypeScript and Go templates. Modules are marked as «module», types as «type», and templates as «template». Go structs are represented as classes, while interfaces use «interface». Struct embedding is shown as composition, since the embedded struct lives and dies with the outer one.

Grey represents existing code, navy represents modified code, and green represents new code. ★ indicates a new member, ✎ indicates a modified one, and the numbered amber notes explain design decisions.

The Mermaid source files are `57-controlled-opposition-class.mmd` and `57-controlled-opposition-sequence.mmd`.

## Sequence Diagram

![Sequence diagram](57-controlled-opposition-sequence.png)

## Q&A

**Class diagram:**

1. Among all the classes shown in the diagram, which 1--2 are most central to understanding the codebase and solving the issue? Explain what role each one plays.

   The two most important are `ShortcutRegistry` and `shortcut.ts`. The registry, introduced in #56, keeps track of shortcuts and handles key presses. Instead of maintaining a separate list, the help dialog gets the current shortcuts through `getShortcuts()`.

   The new logic is in `shortcut.ts`. `initShortcutHelp` registers the `?` shortcut and builds the dialog's contents, while `groupShortcuts` organizes shortcuts by section, putting "General" first.

2. What is the most significant relationship shown in the diagram? Explain what it represents in the system and why it matters for understanding the solution.

   The most important relationship is between `ShortcutRegistry` and `HTMLDialogElement`. Previously, shortcuts could still trigger while a dialog was open. I added a check in `handleKeyDown` to prevent that.

   This stops shortcuts like `s` from focusing the search box behind the dialog and prevents `?` from running again while it's open. The check is in the registry because it works wherever focus is; a listener on the dialog would miss a key pressed while focus is on `body`. It also means future native `<dialog>`s benefit from it without needing their own handling. Gitea's Fomantic modals are plain `<div>`s, so shortcuts still fire behind them.

3. Looking back at your implementation, is there anything in this design you would change, and why?

   I'd make the dialog check more specific. Right now, `dialog[open]` also matches non-modal dialogs, which could unnecessarily disable shortcuts. `dialog:modal` would be more accurate, but happy-dom doesn't properly match it in our unit tests.

   I'd also reconsider generating the shortcut rows with JavaScript template strings if we add more dialogs. It works fine here, but a shared helper might make sense later.

**Sequence diagram:**

1. What user action or system event starts the sequence, and what is the expected outcome when it completes successfully?

   The sequence starts when the page loads and `initShortcutHelp` registers the `?` shortcut. When the user presses `?` outside a text field, the help dialog opens and displays the available shortcuts grouped by section.

   The user can then press Escape to close it and return focus to where it was before.

2. Identify the 2--3 most important steps in the sequence. For each one, describe what is happening and note whether it involves existing code or new/modified code from your solution.

   - **Registering `?`:** The new `initShortcutHelp` function uses the existing `register` method from #56. It associates the shortcut with the dialog on that page.
   - **Opening the dialog:** The new action calls the existing `getShortcuts()`, passes the results through the new `groupShortcuts` function, and opens the dialog with `showModal()`. Reading the registry when the dialog opens ensures recently registered shortcuts are included.
   - **Blocking shortcuts:** I modified the existing `handleKeyDown` to ignore shortcuts while a dialog is open. This prevents shortcuts from affecting the page behind it.

3. What error cases or alternative paths are not shown in the diagram, and why did you leave them out?

   I left out a few paths that either already existed in #56 or behave similarly to what's shown:

   - Pressing `?` in a text field is ignored by the existing field check.
   - Clicking the close button produces the same close event as pressing Escape.
   - Registering another shortcut with `?` triggers the existing conflict error.
   - The initialization steps in `index.ts` are combined into one call to keep the diagram readable.

   These cases don't add much to explaining the changes made in #57.

**Cross-cutting:**

4. If you used AI to create or check any part of the diagrams, describe what it produced, what you verified against the actual code, and what you had to correct or add. If AI was not used, write "N/A."

   I used Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5) to generate both Mermaid diagrams, using the course examples and diagrams from #56 as references. It also rendered them using pele and Playwright.

   The initial diagrams had a few problems, including incorrect method notation, unreadable stereotypes, and section labels colored like design decisions. Claude corrected these and added a separate class for the new dialog.

   I checked the diagrams against the implementation and used the project's mise tasks to verify the code. These tasks build Gitea, run a temporary instance, and test the features in a browser, including the `?` dialog. They also check for unexpected results and JavaScript errors.

=== 56-ab-wm.md
# Issue #56 -- Central keyboard-shortcut registry with chords

## Class Diagram

![Class diagram](56-ab-wm-class.png)

**Notation.** This issue is TypeScript, Vue and Go templates rather than Go, so the diagram maps
them as follows. A TypeScript `class` is a UML class. A module (a file of functions and
module-level variables, such as `shortcut.ts`) is a class with the «module» stereotype: exported
functions are `+`, unexported ones `-`. A TypeScript `type` is a class with «type», a Vue component
is a «component» with its props as attributes, a Go template is a «template» with the attributes it
renders, and a browser custom element is a «custom element». A `data-global-init` attribute that
makes one file run another's code is drawn as a dependency. In Go code the same approach maps a
struct to a class, an interface to an «interface» that structs realize, and struct embedding to
composition.

## Sequence Diagram

![Sequence diagram](56-ab-wm-sequence.png)

## Q&A

**Class diagram:**

1. Among all the classes shown in the diagram, which 1--2 are most central to understanding the codebase and solving the issue? Explain what role each one plays.

   The `ShortcutRegistry`, which is new in this PR, holds every shortcut on a page. Its `register()` function enforces the "clash" rule, which ensures that a set of keys has only one meaning on a page. This class was necessary because, prior to this PR, there was no central place for shortcut handling or behavior, and the HTML of the page itself was the only record of what shortcuts existed. The class also has the `handleKeyDown()` function, which handles all of the key presses.

2. What is the most significant relationship shown in the diagram? Explain what it represents in the system and why it matters for understanding the solution.

   A `Shortcut` can be attached to an `HTMLElement`. This is of utmost importance, especially from the point of view of lifetimes and avoiding clashes. Thanks to this association, the registry notices on its own when the element is no longer on the page (`element.isConnected`). Of course, this led to the introduced tech debt, as "on the page" is not the same as "visible", so a shortcut keeps working, and can still clash, even when its element is hidden.

3. Looking back at your implementation, is there anything in this design you would change, and why?

   There are two changes I would have made, but both would have been "intrusive" or unnecessary for the task at hand:

   - A clashing hint fails loudly and breaks the rest of the page's setup, but avoiding that meant handling the error differently from how the rest of Gitea's setup handles mistakes, which is not ideal.
   - Hidden elements count as present, as noted in 2. The solution could be a visibility check, but that also means key presses would need layout reads, so it is a tough decision to make.

**Sequence diagram:**

1. What user action or system event starts the sequence, and what is the expected outcome when it completes successfully?

   The sequence starts when the user clicks a file in the repository's file tree. This sets up the sequence by first requesting the new content to load in (without reloading the page), and then setting up the page's functionality, which in the process registers the shortcut.

   Once the user presses the key (in this case, t), the listener picks it up and focuses the "Go to file" box.

2. Identify the 2--3 most important steps in the sequence. For each one, describe what is happening and note whether it involves existing code or new/modified code from your solution.

   - The `registerShortcut()` function, which is new in this solution, is the core of the functionality that moved shortcuts from being embedded in the HTML to being centrally managed. It registers the shortcut, along with the details of everything that is needed for the shortcut to function.
   - The other important step is `globalRegistry.handleKeyDown(e)`, which is also new in this solution. It is part of centralizing the shortcuts, where there is now just one function that tracks and handles the processing of relevant key presses. It receives the page's key presses, processes them, and when it finds one it is tracking, sets off the required changes.

3. What error cases or alternative paths are not shown in the diagram, and why did you leave them out?

   A few things were left out: the error during a clash (e.g. a second live T hint), which throws during page setup; the details of how keys are processed, such as two-key sequences and the 1500 ms timeout, since no real page uses a sequence yet and the unit tests cover them; and the first page load, which is essentially just this diagram without the replacement of elements.

**Cross-cutting:**

4. If you used AI to create or check any part of the diagrams, describe what it produced, what you verified against the actual code, and what you had to correct or add. If AI was not used, write "N/A."

   AI (Claude Code, claude-opus-5-5) produced both diagrams, including their callouts, modelled on the course's reference diagrams (hence the similar style).

   For the class diagram, I inspected the diagram to ensure that all the included elements actually make sense; commits were small on purpose, and thus, many of the classes were familiar. For anything I did not understand, I had a quick look through the commits again to see where they came from.

   The sequence diagram was a bit harder, as is the case for most of Gitea's codebase, thanks to its many interacting components. Regardless, many of the events do make sense from the commits I reviewed and the changes they implemented. I also manually traced the `handleKeyDown()` function to see how the key processing happens.

   I did not find a need to change anything after the fact, other than a few guiding notes on scope. This was likely because the AI agent that produced these diagrams also implemented the changes.
```

```text
func prepareUserNotificationsData(ctx *context.Context) {
	pageType := ctx.FormString("type", ctx.FormString("q")) // "q" is the legacy query parameter for "page type"
	page := max(1, ctx.FormInt("page"))
	perPage := util.IfZero(ctx.FormInt("perPage"), 20) // this value is never used or exposed ....
	queryStatus := notificationViewStatus(pageType)
	filter := parseNotificationFilter(ctx)

	countOpts := filter.findOptions(ctx.Doer.ID)
	countOpts.Status = []activities_model.NotificationStatus{queryStatus}
	total, err := db.Count[activities_model.Notification](ctx, countOpts)
	if err != nil {
		ctx.ServerError("ErrGetNotificationCount", err)
		return
	}

	unreadOpts := filter.findOptions(ctx.Doer.ID)
	unreadOpts.Status = []activities_model.NotificationStatus{activities_model.NotificationStatusUnread}
	filteredUnreadCount, err := db.Count[activities_model.Notification](ctx, unreadOpts) // the navbar badge stays global
	if err != nil {
		ctx.ServerError("ErrGetNotificationCount", err)
		return
	}

	viewOpts := filter.findOptions(ctx.Doer.ID)
	viewOpts.Status = []activities_model.NotificationStatus{queryStatus, activities_model.NotificationStatusPinned}
	viewCount, err := db.Count[activities_model.Notification](ctx, viewOpts) // what "select all in this view" acts on
	if err != nil {
		ctx.ServerError("ErrGetNotificationCount", err)
		return
	}

	filterRepos, unreadRepoIDs, err := loadNotificationFilterRepos(ctx, ctx.Doer)
	if err != nil {
		ctx.ServerError("loadNotificationFilterRepos", err)
		return
	}

	pager := context.NewPagination(total, perPage, page, 5)
	if pager.Paginater.Current() < page {
		// use the last page if the requested page is more than total pages
		page = pager.Paginater.Current()
		pager = context.NewPagination(total, perPage, page, 5)
	}

	findOpts := filter.findOptions(ctx.Doer.ID) // pinned rows are filtered like the rest
	findOpts.ListOptions = db.ListOptions{
		PageSize: perPage,
		Page:     page,
	}
	findOpts.Status = []activities_model.NotificationStatus{queryStatus, activities_model.NotificationStatusPinned}
	findOpts.GroupByRepo = filter.GroupByRepo
	nls, err := db.Find[activities_model.Notification](ctx, findOpts)
	if err != nil {
		ctx.ServerError("db.Find[activities_model.Notification]", err)
		return
	}

	var prevPageRepoID int64 // the repository of the previous page's last row, to mark a section that continues
	var groupUnreadCounts map[int64]int64
	if filter.GroupByRepo {
		if page > 1 {
			prevOpts := findOpts
			prevOpts.ListOptions = db.ListOptions{PageSize: 1, Page: (page - 1) * perPage} // the row just before this page
			prev, err := db.Find[activities_model.Notification](ctx, prevOpts)
			if err != nil {
				ctx.ServerError("db.Find[activities_model.Notification]", err)
				return
			}
			if len(prev) > 0 {
				prevPageRepoID = prev[0].RepoID
			}
		}
		if groupUnreadCounts, err = activities_model.CountNotificationsByRepo(ctx, unreadOpts); err != nil {
			ctx.ServerError("CountNotificationsByRepo", err)
			return
		}
	}

	notifications := activities_model.NotificationList(nls)

	failCount := 0

	repos, failures, err := notifications.LoadRepos(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		ctx.ServerError("LoadRepos", err)
		return
	}
	notifications = notifications.Without(failures)
	if err := repos.LoadAttributes(ctx); err != nil {
		ctx.ServerError("LoadAttributes", err)
		return
	}
	failCount += len(failures)
	notifications, failures, err = filterNotificationsByRepoAccess(ctx, ctx.Doer, notifications)
	if err != nil {
		ctx.ServerError("filterNotificationsByRepoAccess", err)
		return
	}
	failCount += len(failures)

	failures, err = notifications.LoadIssues(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		ctx.ServerError("LoadIssues", err)
		return
	}

	if err = notifications.LoadIssuePullRequests(ctx); err != nil {
		ctx.ServerError("LoadIssuePullRequests", err)
		return
	}

	notifications = notifications.Without(failures)
	failCount += len(failures)

	failures, err = notifications.LoadComments(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		ctx.ServerError("LoadComments", err)
		return
	}
	notifications = notifications.Without(failures)
	failCount += len(failures)

	if failCount > 0 {
		ctx.Flash.Error(fmt.Sprintf("ERROR: %d notifications were removed due to missing parts - check the logs", failCount))
	}

	ctx.Data["Title"] = ctx.Tr("notifications")
	ctx.Data["PageType"] = pageType
	ctx.Data["Notifications"] = notifications
	ctx.Data["GroupByRepo"] = filter.GroupByRepo
	if filter.GroupByRepo {
		ctx.Data["NotificationGroups"] = groupNotificationsByRepo(notifications, prevPageRepoID, groupUnreadCounts)
	}
	ctx.Data["Link"] = setting.AppSubURL + "/notifications"
	ctx.Data["SequenceNumber"] = ctx.FormString("sequence-number")
	ctx.Data["FilterRepoID"] = filter.RepoID
	ctx.Data["FilterSource"] = filter.Source
	ctx.Data["IsFiltered"] = filter.IsActive()
	ctx.Data["FilterRepos"] = filterRepos
	ctx.Data["FilterRepoUnread"] = unreadRepoIDs
	ctx.Data["FilteredUnreadCount"] = filteredUnreadCount
	ctx.Data["ViewCount"] = viewCount
	ctx.Data["ViewKey"] = notificationViewLink(pageType, 1, filter) // selections are kept per view, across its pages
	for _, repo := range filterRepos {
		if repo.ID == filter.RepoID {
			ctx.Data["FilterRepo"] = repo // only accessible repos are named, a guessed ID shows the generic label
			break
		}
	}

	pager.AddParamFromRequest(ctx.Req)
	pager.RemoveParam(container.SetOf("div-only", "sequence-number"))
	ctx.Data["Page"] = pager
}

func filterNotificationsByRepoAccess(ctx stdCtx.Context, doer *user_model.User, notifications activities_model.NotificationList) (activities_model.NotificationList, []int, error) {
	failures := make([]int, 0)
	for i, notification := range notifications {
		if notification.Repository == nil {
			continue
		}
		perm, err := access_model.GetIndividualUserRepoPermission(ctx, notification.Repository, doer)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, nil, err
		}
		if !perm.HasAnyUnitAccessOrPublicAccess() {
			failures = append(failures, i)
		}
	}
	return notifications.Without(failures), failures, nil
}

// notificationGroup is one repository's section of the grouped notification list
type notificationGroup struct {
	Repo          *repo_model.Repository
	UnreadCount   int64 // across every page of the view, not only this one
	Continued     bool  // the section started on the previous page
	Notifications activities_model.NotificationList
}

// groupNotificationsByRepo splits a page already ordered by repository into one section per repository
func groupNotificationsByRepo(notifications activities_model.NotificationList, prevPageRepoID int64, unreadCounts map[int64]int64) []*notificationGroup {
	groups := make([]*notificationGroup, 0, 4)
	for _, n := range notifications {
		if len(groups) == 0 || groups[len(groups)-1].Repo.ID != n.RepoID {
			groups = append(groups, &notificationGroup{
				Repo:        n.Repository,
				UnreadCount: unreadCounts[n.RepoID],
				Continued:   len(groups) == 0 && n.RepoID == prevPageRepoID,
			})
		}
		last := groups[len(groups)-1]
		last.Notifications = append(last.Notifications, n)
	}
	return groups
}

// notificationSourceParams maps the "source" query value to the notification source it selects
var notificationSourceParams = map[string]activities_model.NotificationSource{
	"issue":      activities_model.NotificationSourceIssue,
	"pull":       activities_model.NotificationSourcePullRequest,
	"commit":     activities_model.NotificationSourceCommit,
	"repository": activities_model.NotificationSourceRepository,
}

// notificationFilter is the repository and type filter of the notifications page, plus its grouping
type notificationFilter struct {
	RepoID      int64
	Source      string // a key of notificationSourceParams, or "" for any
	GroupByRepo bool   // a view setting, not a filter: it never hides a notification
}

func parseNotificationFilter(ctx *context.Context) notificationFilter {
	filter := notificationFilter{RepoID: max(0, ctx.FormInt64("repo")), GroupByRepo: ctx.FormString("group") == "repo"}
	if source := ctx.FormString("source"); notificationSourceParams[source] != 0 {
		filter.Source = source // unknown values are ignored rather than matching nothing
	}
	return filter
}

func (f notificationFilter) IsActive() bool {
	return f.RepoID != 0 || f.Source != ""
}

func (f notificationFilter) findOptions(userID int64) activities_model.FindNotificationOptions {
	opts := activities_model.FindNotificationOptions{UserID: userID, RepoID: f.RepoID}
	if f.Source != "" {
		opts.Source = []activities_model.NotificationSource{notificationSourceParams[f.Source]}
	}
	return opts
}

// queryValues is built from the parsed values, never the raw request, so redirects only carry validated input
func (f notificationFilter) queryValues() url.Values {
	q := url.Values{}
	if f.RepoID != 0 {
		q.Set("repo", strconv.FormatInt(f.RepoID, 10))
	}
	if f.Source != "" {
		q.Set("source", f.Source)
	}
	if f.GroupByRepo {
		q.Set("group", "repo")
	}
	return q
}
```

```text
// FindNotificationOptions represent the filters for notifications. If an ID is 0 it will be ignored.
type FindNotificationOptions struct {
	db.ListOptions
	IDs               []int64
	UserID            int64
	RepoID            int64
	IssueID           int64
	Status            []NotificationStatus
	Source            []NotificationSource
	UpdatedAfterUnix  int64
	UpdatedBeforeUnix int64
	GroupByRepo       bool // order by repository full name first, so each repository's rows are contiguous across pages
}

// ToCond will convert each condition into a xorm-Cond
func (opts FindNotificationOptions) ToConds() builder.Cond {
	cond := builder.NewCond()
	if len(opts.IDs) > 0 {
		cond = cond.And(builder.In("notification.id", opts.IDs))
	}
	if opts.UserID != 0 {
		cond = cond.And(builder.Eq{"notification.user_id": opts.UserID})
	}
	if opts.RepoID != 0 {
		cond = cond.And(builder.Eq{"notification.repo_id": opts.RepoID})
	}
	if opts.IssueID != 0 {
		cond = cond.And(builder.Eq{"notification.issue_id": opts.IssueID})
	}
	if len(opts.Status) > 0 {
		if len(opts.Status) == 1 {
			cond = cond.And(builder.Eq{"notification.status": opts.Status[0]})
		} else {
			cond = cond.And(builder.In("notification.status", opts.Status))
		}
	}
	if len(opts.Source) > 0 {
		cond = cond.And(builder.In("notification.source", opts.Source))
	}
	if opts.UpdatedAfterUnix != 0 {
		cond = cond.And(builder.Gte{"notification.updated_unix": opts.UpdatedAfterUnix})
	}
	if opts.UpdatedBeforeUnix != 0 {
		cond = cond.And(builder.Lte{"notification.updated_unix": opts.UpdatedBeforeUnix})
	}
	return cond
}

func (opts FindNotificationOptions) ToJoins() []db.JoinFunc {
	if opts.GroupByRepo {
		return []db.JoinFunc{func(sess db.Engine) error {
			sess.Join("INNER", "repository", "repository.id = notification.repo_id")
			return nil
		}}
	}
	return nil
}

func (opts FindNotificationOptions) ToOrders() string {
	if opts.GroupByRepo {
		// case-insensitive like the repository filter's list; the id tiebreak keeps rows from moving between pages
		return "LOWER(repository.owner_name), repository.lower_name, notification.updated_unix DESC, notification.id DESC"
	}
	return "notification.updated_unix DESC"
}

import {toggleElem} from '../utils/dom.ts';

// module state outlives the #notification_div that live refreshes swap in, so a collapsed section stays collapsed;
// it is gone after leaving or paging, which the spec leaves out of scope
const collapsedRepoIDs = new Set<string>();

function setCollapsed(group: HTMLElement, collapsed: boolean) {
  group.querySelector('.notification-group-toggle')!.setAttribute('aria-expanded', String(!collapsed));
  toggleElem(group.querySelector('.notification-group-rows')!, !collapsed);
}

// initNotificationGroups runs for every grouped #notification_table, including the ones swapped in by live refreshes
export function initNotificationGroups(table: HTMLElement) {
  for (const group of table.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('.notification-group')) {
    const repoID = group.getAttribute('data-repo-id')!;
    setCollapsed(group, collapsedRepoIDs.has(repoID));
    group.querySelector('.notification-group-header')!.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
      if ((e.target as Element).closest('a')) return; // the repository name is a link
      const collapsed = !collapsedRepoIDs.has(repoID);
      if (collapsed) {
        collapsedRepoIDs.add(repoID);
      } else {
        collapsedRepoIDs.delete(repoID);
      }
      setCollapsed(group, collapsed);
    });
  }
}

export function initNotificationGroup() {
  registerGlobalInitFunc('initNotificationGroups', initNotificationGroups);
}
```

```text
func (opts *AbsoluteListOptions) GetSkipTake() (skip, take int) {
	return opts.skip, opts.take
}

// FindOptions represents a find options
type FindOptions interface {
	GetPage() int
	GetPageSize() int
	IsListAll() bool
	ToConds() builder.Cond
}

type JoinFunc func(sess Engine) error

type FindOptionsJoin interface {
	ToJoins() []JoinFunc
}

type FindOptionsOrder interface {
	ToOrders() string
}

// Find represents a common find function which accept an options interface
func Find[T any](ctx context.Context, opts FindOptions) ([]*T, error) {
	sess := GetEngine(ctx).Where(opts.ToConds())

	if joinOpt, ok := opts.(FindOptionsJoin); ok {
		for _, joinFunc := range joinOpt.ToJoins() {
			if err := joinFunc(sess); err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
		}
	}
	if orderOpt, ok := opts.(FindOptionsOrder); ok {
		if order := orderOpt.ToOrders(); order != "" {
			sess.OrderBy(order)
		}
	}

	page, pageSize := opts.GetPage(), opts.GetPageSize()
	if !opts.IsListAll() && pageSize > 0 {
		if page == 0 {
			page = 1
		}
		sess.Limit(pageSize, (page-1)*pageSize)
	}

	findPageSize := defaultFindSliceSize
	if pageSize > 0 {
		findPageSize = pageSize
	}
	objects := make([]*T, 0, findPageSize)
	if err := sess.Find(&objects); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return objects, nil
```

```text
Group notifications by repository
Part of #7. Builds on #50 (filter by repository and type) and #51 (bulk actions). Upstream request: go-gitea/gitea#9605.

### User Story

As a user who gets notifications from many repositories, I want to group my notification list by repository so that I can work through one project at a time without filtering to each repository in turn.

### User Scenario

Priya has 45 unread notifications spread across `org/backend`, `org/frontend` and `org/docs`. On the Notifications page she picks "Group by repository". The list turns into one section per repository, each headed by the repository name and its unread count, with that repository's notifications newest first. She collapses `org/docs` to deal with it later, works through `org/backend`, and marks its rows read with the bulk bar from #51. The grouping stays on as the list refreshes and when she moves to page 2, and the URL keeps it, so her bookmark opens the grouped view next time.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given notifications from at least two repositories, when the user selects "Group by repository", then the list shows one section per repository, each headed by the repository's full name and its unread notification count, with the section's rows ordered newest first. The count is the repository's unread notifications under the current filters, across every page and on either tab, and it is hidden when it is 0.
- [ ] AC2: Given grouping is on, when the list loads, then the sections are ordered by repository full name A–Z, and the order does not change when a new notification arrives and the list refreshes.
- [ ] AC3: Given grouping is on and there are more notifications than fit on one page, when the user moves between pages, then every repository's notifications are contiguous, and a section that continues from the previous page repeats its header marked "(continued)".
- [ ] AC4: Given grouping is on, when the user switches between the Unread and Read tabs, changes the #50 repository or type filter, pages, marks a single notification read or pinned, or runs a #51 bulk action, then grouping is still on afterwards (`group=repo` is kept in the URL), and the in-place list refresh keeps it too.
- [ ] AC5: Given grouping is on, when the user activates a section header with the mouse, Enter or Space, then that section collapses or expands, and screen readers announce whether it is expanded. A collapsed section stays collapsed when the list refreshes in place.
- [ ] AC6: Given a pinned notification, when grouping is on, then it is listed inside its repository's section with its pin icon, not in a separate section.
- [ ] AC7: Given grouping is off (the default), when the page loads, then the list looks and behaves exactly as it does today: newest first, no section headers.

### Out of Scope

- Grouping by type or by reason. Reason needs a schema change and stays in #52.
- Per-section actions, such as "Mark this repository as read". The #50 repository filter plus "Mark all as read" already covers this.
- Remembering the grouping choice or collapsed sections between visits, other than through the URL.
- Changes to the notifications API (`/api/v1/notifications`).

### Open Questions

- ~~Should the section header link to the repository?~~ Decided: yes. The name is a link, and the rest of the header toggles the section.
- ~~Should "Select page" in the bulk bar also get a per-section checkbox?~~ Decided: no. "Select page" selects every row on the page, including rows in collapsed sections, as in #51.

### Design Decisions

#### Decision 1: Order grouped notifications by repository in the query, not on the page

**Decision:** When grouping is on, the list query sorts by repository full name and then newest first, and pagination stays at 20 rows per page.
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) Keep the newest-first query and group only the 20 rows already on the page. This is simplest, but one repository shows up on every page in a different spot, which defeats grouping. (b) Turn pagination off when grouping is on, so every group is complete on one page. This is unbounded for users with thousands of read notifications.
**Rationale:** Sorting in the query is the only option that keeps each repository together across pages while keeping page size bounded.
**Consequences:** The notification find options need a sort option, because the order is fixed to `updated_unix DESC` today, and the sort needs a join on the repository. A group can be split across a page boundary, which AC3's "(continued)" header handles.

#### Decision 2: Sections are ordered A–Z, not by most recent activity

**Decision:** Repository sections are ordered alphabetically by full name.
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) Order sections by each repository's newest notification, like the ungrouped list. (b) Order by unread count, highest first.
**Rationale:** The list refreshes in place whenever the unread count changes, so with (a) or (b) the sections would jump around while the user is reading or selecting rows. Alphabetical order stays put, and the user can find a repository where they expect it.
**Consequences:** A busy repository late in the alphabet can sit on page 2 or later. The #50 repository filter is the way to jump straight to it.

#### Decision 3: The grouping choice lives in the URL, like the #50 filters

**Decision:** Grouping is a `group=repo` query parameter, carried through every link, form and refresh the filters already carry.
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) Save it as a per-user setting on the server. (b) Save it in the browser's local storage.
**Rationale:** It matches #50's decision that filters live in the URL: bookmarkable, shareable, and it comes back clean when the user leaves the page. A server setting adds a settings page entry and a write on every toggle for a view preference. Local storage would be invisible to the server-rendered page and the `div-only` refresh.
**Consequences:** Every place that rebuilds the notifications URL (tab links, filter links, pagination, single-row status actions, bulk actions, `div-only` refresh, redirects) has to carry `group`, which is the same set of places #50 changed for `repo` and `source`.

#### Decision 4: Collapsed sections are kept in page memory

**Decision:** The page remembers which sections are collapsed in JavaScript memory and re-applies it whenever the list refreshes in place.
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) Keep the collapsed sections in the URL, for example `collapsed=1,2`, like `group=repo`. (b) Remember nothing, so a refresh expands every section again.
**Rationale:** The list refreshes in place whenever the unread count changes, and that replaces the whole list, so with (b) a section the user collapsed would reopen while they work, which breaks the user scenario. (a) would survive paging and bookmarks, but every link, form and redirect that already carries `repo`, `source` and `group` would have to carry one more parameter, for a preference the Out of Scope section already says is not remembered between visits.
**Consequences:** Collapsed sections reopen when the user moves to another page or leaves the notifications page. Keeping them across pages would mean moving to (a) later.

### Scope
```

```text
async function updateNotificationTable() {
  const notificationDiv = document.querySelector('#notification_div');
  if (!notificationDiv) return;

  try {
    const params = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search);
    params.set('div-only', 'true');
    params.set('sequence-number', String(++notificationSequenceNumber));
    const response = await GET(`${appSubUrl}/notifications?${params.toString()}`);

    if (!response.ok) {
      throw new Error('Failed to fetch notification table');

    const data = await response.text();
    const el = createElementFromHTML(data);

      if (flash && !container.querySelector('.flash-message')) container.prepend(flash);
    }
  } catch (error) {
    console.error(error);
  }
}
```
